prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 – Summary (ideological framing retained)

A secure future built on responsibility, sovereignty and reward for work. The Conservatives argue the economy has turned a corner thanks to firm foundations pre‑Covid and sticking to a clear plan—not Labour’s tax, spend and drift. The choice is lower taxes, lower immigration and protected pensions with the Conservatives; or going back to a fragile, high‑tax, high‑migration status quo under Labour.

- Economy and tax
  - Halve employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish main rate NI for the self‑employed by end of Parliament; no rises in income tax or VAT.
  - Triple Lock Plus: both the State Pension and pensioners’ tax‑free allowance rise by the highest of earnings, inflation or 2.5%.
  - Child Benefit fairness: move to a household test, tapering from £120,000 to £160,000 combined income.
  - 30 hours free childcare from 9 months to school; clamp down on tax avoidance; cut red tape and civil service bloat; keep debt falling under strict fiscal rules.

- Growth, business and Brexit freedoms
  - No rise in corporation tax; maintain full expensing and extend to leasing when affordable.
  - Ten‑point SME plan, business rates relief, prompt payment enforcement, Open Finance expansion.
  - Invest in R&D (£22bn), AI compute, advanced manufacturing; lead in fintech and autos; defend against unfair trade (e.g., EVs from China).
  - Expand trade deals (CPTPP, India, GCC), tough on EU non‑compliance while protecting sovereignty.

- Education, skills and youth
  - Mandate National Service at 18 (military placements or civic service).
  - 100,000 extra apprenticeships funded by closing poor‑value degrees; Advanced British Standard ending the academic/technical divide.
  - Ban mobile phones in school; parental transparency on sex education.

- Welfare and work
  - Make work pay and welfare fair: tighten PIP assessments; overhaul fit notes; tougher sanctions with 12‑month review; finish Universal Credit rollout; fraud crackdown.

- Borders and migration
  - Legal cap on work/family visas that falls each year; raise salary thresholds; health checks/charges before travel.
  - Stop the boats: monthly removals to Rwanda; end legal game‑playing; rewrite asylum rules; more returns deals.

- Defence and security
  - Defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; invest in munitions, innovation and veterans; unwavering support for Ukraine and Trident; tougher stance on hostile states.

- NHS and social care
  - Real‑terms funding rise each year; 92,000 more nurses and 28,000 more doctors; Pharmacy First, more GP surgeries and diagnostics.
  - £3.4bn tech overhaul (NHS App, AI, faster scans); dental reform with NHS service requirement; women’s health boost; implement Cass Review; uphold single‑sex care rights.

- Law, order and community
  - 8,000 more neighbourhood police; facial recognition and hotspot policing; zero tolerance on antisocial behaviour.
  - Tougher sentences for violent/sexual crimes; action on spiking and deepfakes; protect free speech and curb extremist, disruptive protests; robust action against antisemitism and anti‑Muslim hatred.

- Energy, net zero and drivers
  - Pragmatic, affordable net zero by 2050: North Sea annual licensing; treble offshore wind; large nuclear and SMRs; CCS clusters.
  - No new green levies; maintain price cap; energy efficiency vouchers; protect best farmland from solar; retain fracking moratorium.
  - Back drivers: ban road pricing; reverse London ULEZ expansion; local referendums for 20mph/LTNs.

- Housing and infrastructure
  - 1.6 million homes with urban brownfield focus; gentle densification; protect Green Belt.
  - Permanent Stamp Duty relief for first‑time buyers up to £425,000; new Help to Buy; leasehold reform; Renters Reform with anti‑ASB powers.

- Rural, farming, environment and fisheries
  - Farming budget up £1bn; legal food security target; fast‑track farm infrastructure; sensible seasonal labour taper and agri‑tech push.
  - Crack down on water company pollution; invest in flood defences; expand tree planting and access to nature without a blanket Right to Roam; replicate £100m Seafood Fund and back inshore fleets.

- Union and global leadership
  - Strengthen the UK internal market; level up across all nations; accountability for devolved services; deliver Windsor Framework; champion free trade and British values worldwide.
